_comment: Single source of truth for HyperFrames scene templates. Consumed by both the Node engine (hyperframes_engine/) via require() and the Python backend (backend/app/services/visual_learning/) via json.load(). Add/remove/edit a template here instead of editing prompt files or hardcoded lists directly - every consumer derives its behavior from this file. 'status' controls whether the LLM is offered the template: active = offered, banned = deliberately excluded (see 'banned_reason'), fallback_only = never offered to the LLM but used internally as an engine fallback, experimental = offered but flagged as unproven.

column_comparison.best_for: Comparing two items, pros/cons, side-by-side contrast

horizontal_timeline.best_for: Sequences, ordered steps, historical events (prefer this over cycle_template for social-studies chronology/timeline questions)

database_grid.best_for: Structured tabular data, elements, properties, numeric tables

cartesian_grid.template_data_hint: {"title": "...", "equation_label": "ax^2+bx+c=0", "points": [{"x": -2, "y": 4, "label": "Vertex"}], "lines": [], "svg_elements": [{"type": "path", "d": "M 60 300 Q 340 60 620 300", "stroke": "#3b82f6", "stroke_width": 4}]}. The plot area is a FIXED 680x380 SVG viewBox (x: 0-680, y: 0-380, origin top-left) - scale the curve's path 'd' coordinates to fill that range (e.g. spanning roughly x: 40-640, y: 40-340), not an arbitrary/generic scale.

before_after_slider.best_for: State changes, cause vs effect, transformations

quiz_checkpoint.banned_reason: Product decision: lessons should end with a structural summary, not a quiz interruption, per current pedagogy rules.

illustrated_scene.best_for: SVG-drawn scene of a physical/process/anatomical concept (e.g. water cycle with sun+sea+rising vapor, a stomach digesting, a plant cell, a historical scene) - the one template that draws real pictorial content instead of text-in-boxes; prefer this whenever the concept is something students would picture visually
illustrated_scene.template_data_hint: PREFER THIS FIRST - seven generated shapes are available, always prefer one of these over hand-drawing when the concept fits: (0) If the concept is a boundary/structure containing several labeled parts inside it (a parliament building and its roles, a cell and its organelles, a country and its resources, a factory and its departments), use: {"title": "...", "primitive_shape": "enclosure", "primitive_params": {"boundary": {"label": "..."}, "contents": [{"label": "..."}]}} - draws a boundary shape with the listed items arranged inside it in a grid. (1) If the concept is one thing splitting/branching into several parts (an organ and its branches, a river and its tributaries, a family tree, an org chart, a neuron, a blood vessel network), use: {"title": "...", "primitive_shape": "branching", "primitive_params": {"source": {"label": "..."}, "branches": [{"label": "...", "cluster": true|false}]}} - "cluster": true draws a small grape-like circle cluster at that branch's tip (use for things like alveoli/capillaries/leaves - many small terminal parts), false draws a single labeled node (use for things like a named tributary, a family member, a department). (2) If the concept is a SINGLE vessel/organ that items flow into and/or out of - one central thing receiving and passing something on (blood through a heart chamber, a digestive organ receiving and passing on food, migration in/out of a single region) - NOT multiple named components wired to each other (that is node_network, option 5 below - e.g. a circuit with a battery/switch/bulb is node_network, NOT this), use: {"title": "...", "primitive_shape": "container_flow", "primitive_params": {"container": {"label": "..."}, "inflows": [{"label": "..."}], "outflows": [{"label": "..."}]}} - inflows draw as arrows entering from the left, outflows as arrows leaving to the right. (3) If the concept is a PAIR of mirrored organs joined by a central connector (lungs, kidneys, ears, brain hemispheres - exactly two symmetric halves that are physically organ/body-part shaped, not just any two-item comparison), use: {"title": "...", "primitive_shape": "paired_organ", "primitive_params": {"stem": {"label": "..."}, "left": {"label": "..."}, "right": {"label": "..."}}} - draws two mirrored organ-shaped blobs connected to a central stem. (4) If the concept is layers stacked on each other (Earth's core/mantle/crust, atmosphere layers, tiers of government from national to local, geological strata), use: {"title": "...", "primitive_shape": "stacked_layers", "primitive_params": {"layers": [{"label": "..."}], "core_out": true|false}} - list layers innermost-to-outermost with core_out=true for a center-outward concept (Earth's layers, an atom's shells), or top-to-bottom with core_out=false/omitted for a flat hierarchy (tiers of government, social strata). (5) PREFER THIS for any set of multiple named parts/components wired or connected to each other (a circuit with its battery/switch/resistor/bulb, a food web, a trade network, a computer network) - if the concept has several distinct named components connected to one another rather than one single vessel, this is almost always the right choice over container_flow. Use: {"title": "...", "primitive_shape": "node_network", "primitive_params": {"nodes": [{"label": "..."}], "connections": [[0, 1], [1, 2]]}} - nodes are 0-indexed in the order listed; connections are pairs of node indices to draw a line between. (6) If the concept is a central element with several things radiating outward from it (an atom's nucleus and electrons, a solar system, a leader with departments reporting in), use: {"title": "...", "primitive_shape": "radiating_center", "primitive_params": {"center": {"label": "..."}, "satellites": [{"label": "..."}]}}. All seven primitives' geometry is generated by code, not by you, so it is always correctly laid out - just supply the labels and structure. ONLY if the concept does NOT fit any of the seven shapes, fall back to hand-drawing raw elements: {"title": "...", "animation_action": "rise|fall|spin|scale_up|slide_left|slide_right" (how the drawn elements animate in), "elements": [{"type": "path|circle|line|rect", "path_data": "SVG path 'd' attribute, required for type=path", "cx": 640, "cy": 360, "r": 80 (for type=circle), "stroke_color": "#hex", "stroke_width": 2, "fill": "rgba(r,g,b,a)" or "none", "dash_array": "8 6" (REQUIRED on at least one element whenever the scene involves flow/movement - rising vapor, flowing water, wind, current, blood flow, electricity - so it actually animates as flowing rather than sitting static), "label": "optional short text overlay for this element"}]}. The drawing canvas is a FIXED 1280x720 pixel area (x: 0-1280, y: 0-720, origin top-left) - this is NOT a small icon canvas, so scale every coordinate to actually fill it: spread elements across roughly x: 100-1180, y: 100-620, and size circles/shapes generously (radius 40-120px, not 10px) so the scene reads clearly on a full-screen video frame. A tiny cluster of small shapes in one corner is a failure state, not a valid scene. MUST include 6-8 elements combining: an outline/shape (path), 2-3 moving/highlight accents (small circles), and flow indicators (dashed lines) to draw a recognizable, non-lazy scene - 4 elements is the bare structural minimum, not the target; e.g. for the water cycle: a sun (circle) top-right, wavy sea (path) spanning the bottom, 2-3 rising dashed lines for evaporation, a cloud shape (path or grouped circles) top-center, and falling lines for rain.

image_scene.banned_reason: Requires a real image asset pipeline (image_url sourcing) not yet wired up end-to-end.

general_scene.best_for: Free-form fallback only - not a deliberate LLM choice
general_scene.fallback_reason: Used internally by normalizeTemplateId() when an LLM-provided template_id doesn't match any known template. Never offer this to the LLM as a selectable option - if it starts appearing in generated lessons, that indicates a template_id normalization bug, not a valid scene choice.
